faqs.question: Can I track my bus?
faqs.answer: You absolutely can! Click here to search for your trip and start tracking.

faqs.question: What can I bring with me?
faqs.answer: Besides yourself and your thirst for travel, you’re welcome to bring (1) piece of luggage and (1) carry-on bag if you purchase general seating tickets or standard reserved seats. For more information, see our luggage policy .

faqs.question: Can I take my bicycles, skis, snowboards, golf clubs, or musical instruments on board the bus?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately Megabus buses are unable to carry these items unless they are in a case that does not exceed the dimensions stated in the luggage policy . For guidance, this case must not exceed 62 inches when adding the total exterior dimensions of the piece (length + width + height) and should not weigh more than 50 pounds. Megabus cannot store these items if they are out of a case due to the potential for damage to other customers' luggage. Bicycles will be allowed on Coach USA operated trips within the state of Wisconsin .

faqs.question: What do I do if I lost an item on the bus?
faqs.answer: If an item is lost on a bus, a lost item inquiry must be reported to our lost and found department by filling out this form . Once you've submitted the necessary information on the lost item, it will be entered into our system for processing by our lost and found department. Our lost and found department responds to all loss inquiries. The time frame of response may take several days as an investigation to find the lost item must be completed. Megabus makes every attempt to return lost items to their rightful owners and will assist with retrieval to the best of our ability.

faqs.question: Can I bring food on the bus?
faqs.answer: You’re welcome to snack on our buses. However, alcoholic beverages are not permitted on the bus (including checked baggage).

faqs.question: Can I trade in a reservation?
faqs.answer: Sometimes your schedule changes. We get that. We want to ensure you can quickly and easily change your reservation to match your new schedule. You can trade in your reservation online as long as it’s more than 3 hours before your scheduled departure. The cost of your initial reservation will go toward crediting the new one. Please note that there is a trade-in fee applied for changed reservations: $3.00 for trade-ins more than 24 hours from departure. $5.00 for trade-ins 6 to 24 hours from departure. $7.50 for trade-ins 3 to 6 hours from departure. In addition, there is a $3.99 new reservation fee, or $7 when the change is made by telephone, for changed reservations.

faqs.question: Can I cancel and/or get a refund for my reservation?
faqs.answer: Once completed, Megabus reservations cannot be canceled or refunded, but they can be traded in for another journey up to 3 hours before your original scheduled departure. Megabus is not responsible for delays or cancellations caused by traffic, road conditions, weather or other causes over which it has no control. Alternatively where Megabus fails to provide on time-reliable service for reasons wholly within our control refunds, or alternative travel arrangements, may be offered.

faqs.question: Do children/babies need a ticket to travel on Megabus?
faqs.answer: From 0-150, people of all ages are required a ticket to travel with Megabus, children and babies included. Booster/car seats are recommended, but only for children under the age of 5. You’d look pretty silly sitting in your own booster seat.

faqs.question: Can minors ride Megabus unattended?
faqs.answer: Customers under the age of 17 must be accompanied by an adult (17 years or older). If you can pass for 17 (or it’s close), please have your I.D. ready so we can verify your age and ask for your beauty secrets. Unaccompanied minors under the age of 17 are not permitted to travel on Megabus. We recommend that young adults be prepared to produce a photo ID with proof of age to avoid being refused from traveling on our buses.

faqs.question: Where do Megabus routes operate to and from?
faqs.answer: Megabus routes leave from and arrive at strategic locations within the towns and cities we serve . Please note that many stops are curbside, outdoor locations. Details of our departure and arrival points can be found by searching for a trip on our journey planner, and then clicking on the stop details. See additional route details in our top routes section.

faqs.question: Do you offer connecting service between Megabus routes?
faqs.answer: We offer several approved connections and will guarantee your travel to their final destinations on these. These approved connections are available for sale on the Megabus website and will only require one search and one reservation for travel. If you want to book a multiple-connection trip, you’ll have to plan it out and book more than one reservation.

faqs.question: Where can I find the location of my bus stop?
faqs.answer: Hold your index finger out in the air to determine which way the wind is blowing. Look left, and then look right. If you found your bus stop, good job! For everyone else, double-check the address for your arrival/departure location by reviewing your reservation or by searching among our list of bus stops .

faqs.question: How early should I arrive?
faqs.answer: We know that you were so excited for today’s bus trip that you could barely sleep last night. But even still, plan to arrive early – at least 15 minutes early. Everyone wants to get to their destinations on time, so our buses depart at their scheduled time. The last thing we want is to leave you behind like in a bad romantic comedy, other passengers tearfully watching you from the windows, waving sadly goodbye as we pull away.

faqs.question: Still Have Questions?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with our virtual travel assistant, Chuck by emailing questions@us.megabus.com and receive a response within minutes! More contact options

faqs.question: Can I trade in a reservation?
faqs.answer: Sometimes your schedule changes. We get that. We want to ensure you can quickly and easily change your reservation to match your new schedule. You can trade in your reservation online as long as it’s more than 3 hours before your scheduled departure. The cost of your initial reservation will go toward crediting the new one. Please note that there is a trade-in fee applied for changed reservations: $3.00 for trade-ins more than 24 hours from departure. $5.00 for trade-ins 6 to 24 hours from departure. $7.50 for trade-ins 3 to 6 hours from departure. In addition, there is a $3.99 new reservation fee, or $7 when the change is made by telephone, for changed reservations.

faqs.question: How do I trade in a reservation?
faqs.answer: Don’t worry about having to scalp your tickets if you can’t make your bus. As long as it’s more than 3 hours before your scheduled departure, you can trade in your reservation online. Here’s how: 1. Visit megabus.com, click on “ change trip " and enter your order or reservation number along with your email address. 2. Select the reservation you’d like to change and click ‘trade-in.” 3. Follow the on-screen prompts to request a revised reservation using the journey planner menu shown. 4. You did it! We believe bragging rights are in order. To prevent the bus drivers from starting a search party for you when you change reservations, please note that there’s a minor fee applied to modified booking: $3.00 for trade-ins more than 24 hours from departure. $5.00 for trade-ins 6 to 24 hours from departure. $7.50 for trade-ins 3 to 6 hours from departure. In addition, there is a $2.99 new reservation fee, or $7 when the change is made by telephone, for changed reservations.

faqs.question: How will I know if Megabus makes changes to my reservation?
faqs.answer: Megabus will send an e-mail or text message using the information provided, at the time of booking regarding any changes to your service. This may include stop changes, schedule changes, canceled services and weather advisories. This information is also posted on the service advisories section of the website.

faqs.question: Still Have Questions?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with our virtual travel assistant , Chuck by emailing questions@us.megabus.com and receive a response within minutes! More contact options

faqs.question: How do I make a reservation?
faqs.answer: All set to book already? You're good at this! With our new journey planner, making a reservation is as simple as: 1. From our journey planner, first select your departure and arrival city from the drop down menu . Choose either one way or round trip and enter your desired travel dates. 2. Next, enter the number of passengers traveling. Please note that all customers traveling under the same reservation number must board the bus together. Reservations are required for all passengers regardless of age. • Passengers wishing to travel with more than the allotted luggage (See terms and conditions) must purchase additional reservation(s) to accommodate extra luggage. 3. Customers with disabilities must select YES on "assisted travel" if there are any passengers traveling with special requirements. 4. Choose your preferred travel times from the schedules provided. Detailed information regarding your trip and the bus stops can be accessed by clicking on the trip/bus stop links. Please note: When selecting trips that depart after midnight you are required to select the actual date you want to travel, remembering that the date changes at midnight. 5. Choose from available reserved seat options for your trip and click continue. 6. In order to avoid unnecessary charges to your account please review the purchases in your basket and remove any trips added in error before checking out. 7. Review and agree to the terms and conditions . 8. Click pay, and check out using our secure online payment processor, WorldPay. 9. When your reservation has been completed we will issue you an e-mail from WorldPay confirming the acceptance of your payment, and a reservation confirmation e-mail. It is your responsibility to check that the reservation confirmation issued to you is accurate. We are only responsible for issuing the reservation confirmation in line with your request made on this website. Please bring your reservation number with you to board the bus. This is an example of what a Megabus reservation number looks like: 10-1843-090513-M21-1500-WAS-NEW

faqs.question: How do I book a reservation for someone else?
faqs.answer: Looking to buy a Megabus ticket for someone else? Look how selfless you are! Buying a ticket for someone else is simple. First, make your ticket selection on Megabus. Then, during the check out process, you're able to to enter the passenger's email address so that they receive the confirmation email with the trip details. Alternatively, you could enter your own email and send over the confirmation details to the passenger. At time of boarding, have the passenger bring either: a printed copy of their reservation confirmation email or, the reservation number written on a separate piece of paper, or their reservation number shown on their phone. Please keep in mind that passengers under the age of 17 are not permitted to travel on the bus without a parent/guardian that is over the age of 17. While photo identification is not required to board the bus, we recommend that travelers be prepared to produce a photo ID with proof of age to avoid being refused from traveling on our buses due to being underage.

faqs.question: Why should I register for an account with Megabus?
faqs.answer: Don’t checkout as a guest, you mean so much more to us! Plus, we don’t want to have to guess where to send your trip details. It’s totally free and registering for an account means one login for all of your reservations with us. With an account you can: Review upcoming and previous trips in the “my tickets” section. Track the status of your trips under “ change trip .” Save personal details and favorite routes for a quick and easy booking for your next trip. Convinced yet? To register for an account, select “ login ” (duh) from the top of our website, click sign up, and fill out the required fields. You’ll receive an email confirmation with your login and password details. Follow the email instructions, set up your profile and click “save.” You’re all set! Happy travels!

faqs.question: Can I change any of my account details?
faqs.answer: Of course you can - change is good! You can change any of the personal information held related to your name, address, etc. Simply login and select Personal Information from the top menu bar. Make any necessary adjustments and then save your changes.

faqs.question: What if I forget my account password?
faqs.answer: Don't panic! We all forget sometimes. Just click login at the top of our website, click the forgot password link, and follow the instructions provided.

faqs.question: Can I save my credit card information for future purchases?
faqs.answer: Yes. When you make an account with Megabus , you can securely store up to 5 credit cards for faster purchases.

faqs.question: How do I save a credit card to my account?
faqs.answer: When making a purchase, you can save your credit card information to your account by selecting the check box "Save this payment card now to make your next bookings quicker and easier."

faqs.question: How do I remove a credit card from my account?
faqs.answer: In your account settings, displayed next to each payment method, there is an option to "remove." Simply click "remove" and you will be presented with a confirmation message to remove the payment method.

faqs.question: Can I set a primary or default payment method?
faqs.answer: When adding a new payment method, you can set it to be your primary or default payment method by selecting the check box "Set as primary payment card."

faqs.question: How far in advance can I make a reservation?
faqs.answer: Reservations can be made for trips at least 45 days in advance of departure. Due to operational constraints Megabus may choose to change this period.

faqs.question: Why is my desired trip not offered?
faqs.answer: Instant teleportation unfortunately is not yet a reality, so there will be occasional complications when looking for a specific route. This may happen for a couple of reasons. If your travel cities appear, but the calendar dates are grayed out, it may be that the dates you have chosen are too far in advance and are not opened for sale. Check back at a later date to see if the dates are then available. The message "no journeys have been found for the date selected" will appear if all trips have sold out on a particular date. Make your reservations early to avoid disappointment.

faqs.question: How much are Megabus fares?
faqs.answer: All prices are shown in USD . Fares will vary by day and time of travel, time of booking, and demand for seats. Fares are subject to change without notice. Once a reservation is purchased at a specific fare, the fare is not subject to adjustment. A $3.99 reservation fee is charged for all reservations. For trade-ins to existing reservations a $3.00 trade in fee and a $3.99 new reservation fee will apply. Any trade-in to your reservation may result in a fare increase. In general, Megabus will offer its best prices to those who make reservations early. Please note that due to the high sales volumes on our website, prices may fluctuate between searches. Reservations made by telephone will be charged at the same rate as those made on the internet but will be charged a $7.00 reservation fee.

faqs.question: Can minors ride Megabus unattended?
faqs.answer: Customers under the age of 17 must be accompanied by an adult (17 years or older). If you can pass for 17 (or it’s close), please have your I.D. ready so we can verify your age and ask for your beauty secrets. Unaccompanied minors under the age of 17 are not permitted to travel on Megabus. We recommend that young adults be prepared to produce a photo ID with proof of age to avoid being refused from traveling on our buses.

faqs.question: Can I make multiple reservations in one transaction?
faqs.answer: You are able to add multiple trips to your basket by using our journey planner for each trip you wish to purchase. Simply browse back to the journey planner, and choose any additional trips to add to your basket before selecting "pay".

faqs.question: Can I make a reservation using a mobile device?
faqs.answer: You sure can. Megabus is accessible from any smart phone or other mobile device.

faqs.question: How do I know my payment was accepted?
faqs.answer: Please check your email inbox for the Wordpay confirmation email and megabus reservation confirmation email. If you have received both of these then your transaction was successful. If not, please check to see if the information we sent to you is in your junk mail/spam folders. If you only receive a Worldpay confirmation e-mail, and not a reservation confirmation please contact us at 877-462-6342. If you do not receive either e-mail within an hour of purchase please contact us at 877-462-6342.

faqs.question: Will I get a confirmation for my reservation?
faqs.answer: After completing your payment, a confirmation page will display your Megabus reservation numbers. Please print this page as a record of your transaction. It is your responsibility to check that the confirmation issued to you is accurate. We are only responsible for issuing the confirmation in line with your request made on this website. Megabus will also send you an e-mail or text message using the information provided at the time of booking in case you don't have access to a printer while making your reservations. In order to board the bus you must present your reservation number provided in the confirmation page. You are required to arrive at the pickup location 15 minutes prior to your departure time.

faqs.question: What is my reservation number?
faqs.answer: We don’t expect you to speak in code. Our bus drivers can translate your reservation number for you. Your reservation number will be a combination of numbers and letters and can be obtained from the confirmation page displayed after finalizing your Megabus purchase. A copy of your reservation information is also sent to the e-mail address provided at the time of booking. Reservations are only valid on the trip(s) date, time, origin and destination as stated on the reservation. This is an example of what a reservation looks like. 10-1843-090513-M21-1500-WAS-NEW

Megabus is not responsible for delays or cancellations caused by traffic, road conditions, weather or other causes over which it has no control. Alternatively where Megabus fails to provide on time-reliable service for reasons wholly within our control refunds, or alternative travel arrangements, may be offered.

faqs.question: How will I know if Megabus makes changes to my reservation?
faqs.answer: Megabus will send an e-mail or text message using the information provided at the time of booking regarding any changes to your service. This may include stop changes, schedule changes, canceled services and weather advisories. This information is also posted on the service advisories section .

faqs.question: Do children/babies need a ticket to travel on Megabus?
faqs.answer: From 0-150, people of all ages are required a ticket to travel with Megabus, children and babies included. Booster/car seats are recommended, but only for children under the age of 5. You’d look pretty silly sitting in your own booster seat.

faqs.question: How do I pay for my trip?
faqs.answer: We appreciate a good haggle like anyone else, but for now, we only accept payments using major credit cards. All Megabus prices are shown in USD. Payment for reservations can be made using major credit cards, including Visa, MasterCard, and American Express. Unfortunately Megabus reservations cannot be paid for in cash or by check. Please note that some credit card issuers and banks may charge for transactions made outside your geographical area (international transaction fee). These fees are charged by your card issuer/bank and not Megabus. Please check with your card issuer if you are unsure as Megabus cannot be held liable for any such charges. Once you have selected your trip(s) you will be taken to the Worldpay page to pay for your reservation. Enter the necessary details and make your payment. WorldPay is our trusted and secure online payment processor. In an age where protecting online credit card information is so critical, we have made a strategic decision to team up with WorldPay. Please be aware that Megabus does not hold any credit card information on file. Each purchase will require re-entering your payment information.

faqs.question: How should I plan a multiple city-city trip?
faqs.answer: So you want to take more than one Megabus bus? Look at you, Mr. or Ms. Traveler. We can take you across so many states that you’ll run out of phone camera storage. But there a few things you should know first. If you are building your own trip from city to city then all it takes is a bit of careful planning. You can take a trip from, say, Toronto to San Antonio, but you’d have to change buses a few times to get there, so bring your toothbrush, some food, and a good book or movie (how long has it been since you’ve seen every Rocky movie?) Connecting trip tips Make sure you leave at least two hours between a scheduled arrival and the next departure. Sometimes there’s heavy traffic or inclement weather and we don’t want you to miss your connecting bus Plan your potential layovers, which can be lengthy depending on bus schedules, and be ready to chat to lots of fellow travelers along the way (they’ll appreciate the fact you brought your toothbrush too!)

faqs.question: Where can I find more information about weather cancellations?
faqs.answer: Stay up-to-date on weather related cancellations and be informed on all Megabus news, contests, and announcements by following us on Facebook or Twitter/Instagram @megabus. In addition, under the “ change trip ” section of the website, you can enter your reservation number to view potential route cancellations. We also post updates on our service advisories page.

faqs.question: Still Have Questions?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with our virtual travel assistant, Chuck by emailing questions@us.megabus.com and receive a response within minutes! More contact options

faqs.question: How do I make a reservation?
faqs.answer: Customers with special requirements can easily book a ticket on Megabus. After filling out your trip details in our journey planner, click on the "assisted travel" option, and answer a few simple questions that will allow us to do our very best to accommodate you. Customers are also welcome to call 1-877-GO2-MEGA (1-877-462-6342) to have one of our dedicated customer service representatives assist them with their reservation.

faqs.question: Can you accommodate passengers with disabilities?
faqs.answer: Megabus is fully ADA compliant, welcomes all customers, and does not discriminate based on disability. Our courteous, professional, and experienced drivers are committed to ensuring you have a safe, comfortable trip. Megabus provides accessible transportation service to those with special requirements, including, but not limited to, those with walking difficulties or sight impairments, those who use mobility units and customers with service animals and breathing aids.

faqs.question: Can I take animals on board the bus?
faqs.answer: Whether the animals purchased a ticket or not (good job training!), we're unable to carry animals onboard, with the exception of trained service animals that assist customers with their travel. Service animals must be properly harnessed and under the direct control of the passenger at all times.

faqs.question: Are there any limitations on the size of a mobility unit?
faqs.answer: Each Megabus double-decker bus has space for two mobility units. Mobility units can be accommodated up to 30 inches wide and 48 inches long and are acceptable weighing up to 600 pounds when occupied.

faqs.question: Who do I contact if my disability request was not honored?
faqs.answer: Megabus is obligated to provide accessible transportation service to customers with disabilities. If you believe that Megabus has failed to fulfill this obligation or that you have been discriminated against on the basis of your disability, please contact Kat Montilla in any of the following ways: 1. Email: k.montilla@coachusa.com 2. Telephone: 908-372-6195 3. Fax: 908-994-9423 4. Mail: 349 First Street, Elizabeth, New Jersey 07206.

faqs.question: What do I need to know about boarding the bus?
faqs.answer: Locate your arrival/departure location, which was emailed to you with your confirmation number. (It can also be viewed by visiting our change trip section . Arrive at least 15 minutes prior to your scheduled departure. Speak with a Megabus representative prior to departure and they will happily assist you with boarding, when appropriate Each Megabus driver is trained and experienced with boarding and securing a variety of mobility devices.

faqs.question: Still Have Questions?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with our virtual travel assistant , Chuck by emailing questions@us.megabus.com and receive a response within minutes! More contact options

faqs.question: What are Megabus' terms and conditions?
faqs.answer: See our full terms and conditions .

faqs.question: Still Have Questions?
faqs.answer: Get in touch with our virtual travel assistant, Chuck by emailing questions@us.megabus.com and receive a response within minutes! More contact options

faqs.question: What is my reservation number?
faqs.answer: We don’t expect you to speak in code. Our bus drivers can translate your reservation number for you. Your reservation number will be a combination of numbers and letters and can be obtained from the confirmation page displayed after finalizing your Megabus purchase. A copy of your reservation information is also sent to the e-mail address provided at the time of booking. Reservations are only valid on the trip(s) date, time, origin and destination as stated on the reservation. This is an example of what a reservation looks like. 10-1843-090513-M21-1500-WAS-NEW

faqs.question: What do I give the driver when boarding the bus?
faqs.answer: Besides a kind greeting, passengers are required to present a valid reservation number, provided at the time of purchase, when boarding Megabus. While not required, we do suggest you bring a printed copy of your reservation confirmation email, as this will include your reservation number(s). No physical tickets are issued for travel. Your WorldPay transaction ID # or your order # will not be accepted as proof of a reservation. Make sure that you obtain a reservation number for each trip you reserve . Reservations are only valid on the trip(s) date, time, origin and destination as stated on the reservation. If we have reason to suspect the fraudulent use of a reservation confirmation, we reserve the right to refuse travel on our vehicles. No refund will be made in relation to any reservation confirmation refused due to fraudulent use. As unaccompanied children under the age of 17 are not permitted to travel on Megabus, we recommend that young adults be prepared to produce a photo ID with proof of age to avoid being refused from traveling on our buses.

faqs.question: What are the bag size requirements?
faqs.answer: To make sure your luggage dimensions are in check, please keep in mind the below parameters: Because our drivers aren’t looking for a free workout, your luggage cannot exceed 50 pounds . Why? We have to lift them! To avoid us trying to play Tetris with your belongings, remember that all luggage cannot exceed 62 inches in total (length + width + height). One small carry-on bag is permitted, but it has to be small enough to fit under the seat in front of you (think briefcase, backpack, or laptop bag).

faqs.question: What can I bring with me?
faqs.answer: Besides yourself and your thirst for travel, you’re welcome to bring (1) piece of luggage and (1) carry-on bag if you purchase general seating tickets or standard reserved seats. For more information, see our luggage policy .

faqs.question: What can’t I bring?
faqs.answer: Again, our drivers appreciate the workout, but no pieces of luggage over 50 pounds are permitted – regardless of whether additional reservations have been purchased. Cycling enthusiasts are welcome, but bicycles are not permitted unless they are inside a case that meets the luggage allowance . Alcohol, drugs, and weapons are strictly prohibited on our buses (including checked luggage).

faqs.question: Can I take my bicycles, skis, snowboards, golf clubs, or musical instruments on board the bus?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately Megabus buses are unable to carry these items unless they are in a case that does not exceed the dimensions stated in the luggage policy . For guidance, this case must not exceed 62 inches when adding the total exterior dimensions of the piece (length + width + height) and should not weigh more than 50 pounds. Megabus cannot store these items if they are out of a case due to the potential for damage to other customers' luggage. Bicycles will be allowed on Coach USA operated trips within the state of Wisconsin.

faqs.question: Can I bring food on the bus?
faqs.answer: You’re welcome to snack on our buses. However, alcoholic beverages are not permitted on the bus (including checked baggage).

faqs.question: Can I smoke on the bus?
faqs.answer: Look outside! You’ll see that there are already plenty of clouds in the sky. For the safety and comfort of other passengers, please wait until a rest stop for smoking and vaping as they are prohibited.

faqs.question: Are the Megabus buses equipped with seatbelts?
faqs.answer: All Megabus operated buses are equipped with seatbelts. Children under the age of 7 are recommended to use a child safety seat that meets applicable government regulations for motor vehicle use and is in a state of good repair. Please note that for operational reasons Megabus may need to substitute a replacement vehicle which may not have seatbelts.

faqs.question: My trip involves crossing the Canadian/US border – does it require my passport?
faqs.answer: Persons traveling across the U.S./Canadian border should research information on documents needed to cross the border from the relevant U.S. and Canadian government agencies; as such requirements are subject to change. A valid passport is required for citizens of any nation, including citizens of the United States and Canada, to cross the border in either direction between the United States and Canada. Passengers are advised to consult with their government if they seek to cross the border without a valid passport. For U.S. Government information, passengers should consult with U.S. Customs and Border Protection at www.cbp.gov. For Canadian Government information, passengers should consult with Citizenship and Immigration Canada at www.cic.gc.ca. A guardian traveling with children must provide proof of custody or notarized parental authorization for travel. An adult accompanying a child who is neither a parent nor guardian of the child should have written permission from a parent or guardian to accompany the child across the border, including the name and contact information of the parent or guardian.

faqs.question: What should I know about crossing the border?
faqs.answer: Let’s give the border guards a break and make their jobs easy. Know that all luggage is subject to inspection when crossing international borders. You will be asked to declare any items subject to duty upon crossing the border. Passengers must claim their luggage at the border crossing point for clearance through customs before being allowed to proceed across the border. No luggage is allowed across the border unless claimed by a passenger.

faqs.question: What if I miss my schedule departure?
faqs.answer: Much like the airline industry, all Megabus seats are sold on a reservation basis and you must travel at your specified time and date. Customers are required to be at their departure point at least 15 minutes before their selected trip is scheduled to depart. This allows Megabus drivers to board customers in a timely manner avoiding any delays that may impact the departure of the vehicle. No refunds or credits will be given in instances where customers miss the bus; however, reservations can be changed on our website up until 6 hours prior to departure.

faqs.question: What do I do if I lost an item on the bus?
faqs.answer: If an item is lost on a bus, a lost item inquiry must be reported to our lost and found department by filling out this form . Once you've submitted the necessary information on the lost item, it will be entered into our system for processing by our lost and found department. Our lost and found department responds to all loss inquiries. The time frame of response may take several days as an investigation to find the lost item must be completed. Megabus makes every attempt to return lost items to their rightful owners and will assist with retrieval to the best of our ability.

faqs.question: What about lost luggage?
faqs.answer: While we don’t offer GPS tracker technology to attach to your luggage just yet, our maximum liability to you for any loss or damage to your luggage is US $250 per passenger. Of course, Megabus will only be responsible to reimburse passengers up to the maximum liability limit in the event of negligence on our part.

faqs.question: Does Megabus have liability/travel insurance?
faqs.answer: Megabus has purchased insurance in accordance with our legal responsibility. All legal liabilities to third parties, to include damage to property and personal injury are covered. Megabus does not offer travel insurance. If you wish to purchase travel insurance for your trip, then please speak to your insurance provider.

faqs.question: How long are the breaks for rest stops?
faqs.answer: Listen to your driver’s announcement prior to departing the bus. He or she will let you know how much time you have at the rest area before needing to be back onboard. Please return promptly to ensure you arrive to your destination on time.

faqs.question: How should I prepare for weather?
faqs.answer: Depends how much of a survivalist you are. For those who would rather brave the great outdoors responsibly, check the weather prior to departing home. Dress appropriately for the conditions and bring an umbrella if it’s expected to rain. For hot days, we recommend light clothing or refreshing beverages to take on board.

faqs.question: What happens in the case of a weather disruption to service?

sections.body:
New York City : Big-City Energy in Just a Weekend 
 Fewer places can pack as much into a weekend as New York City. No other place offers the country’s most famous landmarks, Broadway shows, the coolest pizza places, shopping, and neighborhoods with their own personalities like NYC. This is the place you can visit multiple times and still find something new. 

 For a weekend trip, focus on a few areas rather than trying to cram everything in. Central Park and Midtown, Greenwich Village or SoHo, Lower Manhattan and the Brooklyn Bridge are the best combinations you can explore on a weekend.  

 Hidden gem: Roosevelt Island 

 The Roosevelt Island Tram gives you a different perspective and view of the East River and Manhattan skyline. Once you’re on the island, take a walk along the waterfront to the Four Freedoms Park. 

 Don’t miss: 

- Central Park 

- Times Square and Broadway

 Philadelphia : History, Food, and Neighborhood Charm 
 Philadelphia gives you a mix of American history, great food, and lively neighborhoods. It’s an easy city to explore on a weekend trip. You can spend part of your trip seeing some of the country’s most famous historic sites, and then spend the rest exploring local markets, museums, restaurants, and beautiful green spaces. 

 If you go to Old City, you can see Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, and then wander around the historic streets. Reading Terminal Market is the best spot to get a taste of Philly’s food scene. You can end your weekend exploring the murals around the city and spend the afternoon in neighborhoods like Rittenhouse Square and Fishtown. 

 Hidden gem: Elfreth’s Alley 

 Elfreth’s Alley is one of the oldest residential streets in the US, located in Old City. It’s a beautiful scene with colorful historic homes and a cobblestone street. Just a short walk from the city’s busiest attractions, Elfreth’s Alley is the perfect space for a quieter glimpse into Philadelphia’s history.

 Spend some time exploring Georgetown’s historic streets. You can stroll along the waterfront and then go to one of the lively neighborhoods for dinner and drinks. The National Gallery of Art and the U.S. Capitol area are great spaces to explore, and there are many free attractions you can walk between as well.

 If you want to maximize your 48 hours in New York City, you should aim to get there in the morning, ideally around 8 to 10 AM. This gives you enough time to check in, drop off your bags, grab breakfast, and start exploring without wasting half the first day.

sections.heading: Day 1: Midtown Manhattan and NYC’s Iconic Sights
sections.body:
Now that you know when and how to get to New York, we can start to plan your first day. Your first 24 hours in New York City are all about exploring the city classics. You’d want to aim to keep your plans centered around Midtown Manhattan and Central Park. This area is easy to navigate and has the city’s more recognizable landmarks. 

 Morning: Central Park 
 The first part of your morning will be spent settling into your accommodation. Once you’re done, head over to Central Park. Honestly, you dont need to explore the entire park in 48 hours in New York City. Focus more on the southern section and look for landmarks like Bethesda Terrace, the Mall, and Bow Bridge. 

 Once you’ve consumed enough of the park’s glory, grab some breakfast and coffee nearby and then make your way toward midtown. 

 Afternoon: Fifth Avenue and Rockefeller Center 
 Fifth Avenue is one of New York’s most famous streets where you can find luxury stores, iconic landmarks, and beautiful architecture. It’s a great place to explore on your first visit to New York City. Make sure to take as many pictures of the Empire State Building when you reach 34th Street. If you have the time, you can also go up to its observation deck. 

 After Fifth Avenue, head to Rockefeller Center, where you can find the famous plaza and Radio City Music Hall. Then, head up to Top of the Rock for astonishing panoramic views of Manhattan. Once you’re done with the area, continue your route toward Grand Central Terminal. Its famous Main Concourse and Beaux-Arts architecture are the highlights you’d want to check out before grabbing lunch or a snack somewhere nearby. 

 Evening: Times Square and Broadway  
 NYC nights are the perfect time to spend in Times Square. Make your way there in the evening to see the bright billboards and nonstop energy of the city that never sleeps. 

 A great spot to have dinner is the Theater District, and if you're up for it, finish your evening by catching a Broadway show. This is one of the most iconic forms of entertainment in the city and an exciting experience for first-time visitors.

sections.heading: Day 2: Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn
sections.body:
The first half of your 48 hours in New York City is over, and you’ve already seen and experienced most of the city’s important landmarks. Day 2 takes you south through Lower Manhattan before moving on to Brooklyn for New York’s best skyline views. We’ll cover other significant landmarks of the city, the magnificent Brooklyn Bridge, and finish the itinerary with a relaxed evening by the waterfront. 

 Morning: Lower Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty 
 Start the morning at Battery Park, the perfect place for admiring views of the Statue of Liberty. If you plan to visit Liberty Island itself, book an early ferry and set aside several hours for this mini-trip. If not, opt for the Staten Island Ferry (free of charge) to get great views of the Statue of Liberty without spending hours of your day. 

 From Battery Park, walk through the Financial District where you can find famous landmarks like Wall Street, the New York Stock Exchange, and the Charging Bill. 

 Afternoon: 9/11 Memorial and Brooklyn Bridge 
 Continue your day by visiting the 9/11 Memorial, where you can take some time to visit the reflecting pools and pay your respects. You can also visit the 9/11 Memorial Museum nearby. Allow some extra time to learn more about the events and their impact. 

 After that, head over to the Brooklyn Bridge. Walking across the bridge should take about 30 to 60 minutes, depending on how often you wish to stop for breaks or photos. From the bridge, you’ll see one of the most impressive views of the Manhattan skyline and the East River. 

 Evening: DUMBO and Brooklyn Waterfront 
 After crossing the bridge and reaching Brooklyn, explore DUMBO. DUMBO is advertised as one of the borough’s most photogenic neighborhoods, a place that’s all about love for NYC. The best activities here are walking along the waterfront, taking the famous Manhattan Bridge photo (Washington Street between Front and Water Streets), and enjoying the views from Brooklyn Bridge Park. 

 As your 48 hours in New York City come to an end, end this memorable trip with dinner in Brooklyn, then head back to Manhattan for one last look at the city skyline. After two busy days, this is the perfect time to slow down and soak up your last few hours in New York.

sections.heading: Tips for Your First 48 Hours in New York City
sections.body:
Two days in New York can go by without you even noticing. That’s why the 2-day New York itinerary is important to ensure you enjoy every bit of your time. These tips will help you plan your trip even better: 

- Plan by neighborhood: Group attractions that are close to each other in one cluster to avoid wasting time crossing the city. 

- Book popular attractions ahead: If you need tickets for some activities, like seeing a Broadway show or visiting the Statue of Liberty, book your tickets before your trip to avoid lines and complications. 

- Start early: Popular sights and landmarks are quieter in the morning. Planning those early means you get more time to explore. 

- Wear comfortable shoes: Most of your time in NYC is spent walking or riding public transportation. Wearing comfortable shoes makes it easier to navigate the city. 

- Use the subway: The NYC subway is one of the fastest and most convenient ways to get around the city. 

- Leave room for spontaneity: Don’t plan activities for every single minute of the day. Some of the best NYC moments happen when you are simply wandering around.

 Travel on less busy days

 Stay flexible with your travel date

 Check your departure and arrival locations

sections.heading: Bus Tickets To Washington DC : What To Expect?
sections.body:
Traveling by bus is often the cheapest way to reach Washington, D.C. Standard tickets usually cost from $19, depending on the time, departure location, and the type of carrier you choose. 

 If you want to get the best deals, plan and book your tickets at least 2-4 weeks before you want to travel. Avoid last-minute booking as they may get significantly overpriced, especially during holidays or the festive season.  

 Here are some tips on getting a cheap bus to Washington: 

- Book 2 to 4 weeks ahead 

- Compare multiple bus companies 

- Travel Tuesday to Thursday 

- Consider early morning or late-night departures 

- Use comparison websites to find the best rate

sections.heading: Arriving in Washington DC: Know The Area
sections.body:
When you arrive in Washington, DC, you will most probably end up in Union Station, which is Washington’s central arriving point located north of the United States Capitol. It offers direct Metro Red Line access, easy downtown walking, and clear signs to bus bays.  

 Taxis and rideshares wait outside the main entrance, and travelers have plenty of shops, dining, and seating inside. You will get everything you need right at the bus station, making your arrangements convenient.  

 Tips for when you arrive: 

- Follow the signs to the bus bays or main hall. Union Station is large and busy, so check your bus ticket or arrival screen to make sure you’re heading in the right direction. 

- If you want to start exploring right away, you're in luck. The U.S. Capitol, National Mall, and several museums are just a short walk from the station. 

- Travel light if possible. The station can get crowded, and navigating with heavy luggage, especially during peak hours, can slow you down. 

- Use the Metro for quick connections. The Red Line runs through Union Station, making it easy to reach other neighbourhoods without a rideshare. 

- Union Station has plenty of cafes, restrooms, and seating areas where you can regroup before heading out.

sections.heading: How To Get Around Washington DC
sections.body:
Once you arrive, getting around Washington, D.C. is surprisingly easy. The city has an efficient Metro system and a wide network of buses that connect most major attractions, making it simple to move between neighbourhoods without needing a car. If you prefer exploring at your own pace, D.C. is also very walkable and offers plenty of bike lanes and scooter rentals. For door-to-door convenience, taxis and rideshares are available throughout the city. 

 If you need extra help navigating, download the DC Metro Map App to check train times, routes, and service updates. With so many transportation options, you can get wherever you need to go comfortably and affordably.

sections.heading: Megabus Recommendation: What to Do in Washington
sections.body:
Washington, D.C. has so much to see! Here are the top 5 things to do: 

- Tour the iconic White House 

- Explore the Smithsonian museums 

- Walk the historic National Mall 

- Visit the Library of Congress 

- Pay your respects at Arlington National Cemetery 

If you’re a history lover, D.C. is the perfect place to explore. Beyond the must-see Smithsonian museums, check out the National Archives to view the Constitution, the National Museum of African American History and Culture, and the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. If you enjoy art, don’t miss the National Gallery of Art, The Phillips Collection, and the Kennedy Centre’s vibrant performing arts scene.

sections.heading: Where To Stay In Washington DC?
sections.body:
If you arrive by bus and want a comfortable, convenient place to crash, D.C. offers plenty of great stays across different budgets 

- Waldorf Astoria, The Willard InterContinental, and The Hay‑Adams will bring luxury to your stay. 

- Embassy Suites by Hilton, Hotel Zena, and Hilton Garden Inn are some mid-range stay options with good amenities at reasonable prices. 

- Washington Plaza Hotel provides safe, clean basics and low-cost options for those who want comfort on a budget.

sections.heading: Where to shop in Washington DC?
sections.body:
Though the city boasts the National Mall, you won’t find many shopping options there. Not to worry, though, as there are plenty of places to do so! 

 Make sure to hit up CityCenterDC on your trip to Washington DC. Newly built and containing over 10 acres of stores and restaurants, it’s a great space for all of your retail and culinary needs.  

 However, you can’t talk about shopping in Washington, DC, without mentioning Georgetown. Georgetown features small independent shops, high-end boutiques, restaurants, and all sorts of other stores. Make sure to grab a famous Georgetown cupcake on your trip to Washington, DC, assuming the line isn’t around the block!

sections.heading: Nightlife in Washington DC
sections.body:
Washington, DC, may be known for its history, but the city comes alive at night. If you’re in the mood for cocktails, Off the Record at the Hay-Adams is a local favourite, known for its political décor and well-crafted drinks. Beer lovers should check out ChurchKey, which offers more than 500 varieties and great bar food.  

 If live music is more your style, The Black Cat is a standout venue featuring indie bands, DJs, and energetic late-night shows perfect for ending your D.C. trip on a fun note.

sections.body:
After traveling by bus to Des Moines, you’ll arrive at the Des Moines Bus Depot on 1641 E. Euclid Ave . This is the main intercity bus terminal in Des Moines. What makes this bus station special is that it’s located in Highland Park (north-central area,) which is a residential area rather than the touristic downtown. You get to see everyday life happening as soon as you arrive!

 Des Moines Bus Depot is a proper bus station rather than a curb-side bus stop, which means you can expect standard amenities from the station. Several transit lines, like DART bus lines 50 and 16, are nearby, and you can travel throughout the city right from the station.

 Since the Des Moines Bus Depot is not close to any tourist attractions and landmarks, choosing your accommodation close to the bus station could cause some issues. Just ensure you keep traffic in mind when travelling to downtown and visiting the city’s attractions.

sections.heading: Transportation Options in Des Moines
sections.body:

If you’re traveling between suburbs and downtown, especially during rush hours, DART offers Express Route buses that skip many stops and use freeways.

 In areas that are not covered by the fixed routes, DART offers On-Call or Flex Connect services. These are shared-ride or demand-based options for when you’re outside the main grid or traveling off-peak!

 Another cool factor about DART? They offer Paratransit ( Bus Plus ) for travelers with mobility limitations. These services are door-to-door, wheelchair-accessible rides.

 And of course, you can always use taxis and ridesharing apps to get around the city if there are no available buses or you prefer not to use them.

sections.heading: Arriving in Detroit: Know the Area

After your bus to Detroit trip, you’ll arrive at the Detroit Bus Station on 1001 Howard Street . This is the city’s main transportation hub, with indoor waiting areas, restrooms, ticket counters, and seating. Overall, it’s a comfortable first stop after your long bus ride.

 Detroit Bus Station (also known as the Howard Street Station ) is close to Detroit’s historic Corktown neighborhood, west of downtown, which means you’ll be close to cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores, all within walking distance!

 From the Howard Street Station, getting around is fairly easy, thanks to the Detroit Department of Transportation system. Many DDOT bus routes stop nearby; you can use them to get to downtown and around the city. Taxis and rideshares are also available from the station, and landmarks like the Detroit Riverfront, Campus Martius Park are a short ride away if you want to start exploring right away.

sections.heading: Tips for when you arrive:
sections.body:

sections.heading: Transportation Options in Detroit
sections.body:
The Detroit Department of Transportation is the city’s main bus network, with routes throughout Detroit. It’s a great option for getting around town. QLINE Streetcar system also connects neighborhoods such as downtown, midtown, New Center, and more. It’s perfect for shorter trips between different areas .

 Another convenient option is the Detroit People Mover , a small elevated rail loop that’s perfect for getting around downtown quickly. If you’re visiting multiple nearby attractions, the DPM is your most suitable option.

 You can also share a bike or use a scooter around for short trips and enjoy beautiful days. You’ll have more flexibility and can enjoy a more local vibe. Taxis and rideshares are always available around the city if the public transportation system doesn’t cover where you need to go.

sections.heading: Megabus Recommendation: What to Do in Detroit
sections.body:

- Take the Ford Rouge Factory Tour

 Numerous tours can help you navigate downtown and around the city. There are plenty of attractions to explore, like Greektown, Detroit Eastern Market, or the Motown Historical Museum. Detroit is the travel destination for exploring historic architecture.

sections.heading: Where to Stay
sections.body:
When you arrive by bus to Detroit, you’ll have many accommodation options. We classified some of the city’s greatest hotels into luxury, mid-range, and affordable choices:

 You have two amazing options for a luxurious stay. The Godfrey Hotel Detroit is a stylish and modern hotel located in Corktown and offers a rooftop lounge, restaurant and bar, and easy access to the city’s nightlife spots. Shinola Hotel is also a comfortable stay in downtown, with beautifully designed interiors, a lobby bar, and a nod to Detroit's historic vibe.

 For a more affordable, mid-range option, you can choose the Siren Hotel , a boutique-style hotel that merges old-building history with modern touches. With the Siren Hotel, you’ll get comfort, style, and personality at a reasonable price.

 If you value comfort but are on a budget, the Trumbull and Porter Hotel Detroit and Red Roof Inn Detroit – Warren are great options that offer comfortable and stylish rooms at affordable prices. The Red Roof Inn is a bit outside the city center, perfect for travellers who plan to spend most of their time exploring rather than staying in the hotel.

sections.heading: Where to Shop
sections.body:
Detroit is not just about cars and history; you’ll find lots of shopping opportunities in the city that are simply not to be missed!

 Greektown is known as Detroit’s most ethnic neighborhood. You’ll find a great variety of boutiques and specialty shops there. The Riverfront Shops inside the GM Renaissance Center offer a wide array of shopping options as well.

 And of course, no trip to Detroit will be complete without visiting the historic Detroit Eastern Market , with more than 150 food vendors and shops, offering some of the greatest food in the city!

sections.heading: Nightlife in Detroit
sections.body:
Traveling by bus to Detroit doesn’t end in visiting museums and parks. Detroit is known as one of the greatest beer-brewing states in the US, and for its musical scene!

 Motor City Brewing Works is a local, renowned microbrewery where you can enjoy the best beer in the city. If you prefer cocktails over beers, visit the Skip downtown for a cocktail bar and chic atmosphere. The Ghost Bar , however, offers you beautiful architecture and history along with drinks.

 You can’t miss the music of Detroit. Visit Cliff Bell’s for live music, or catch a show at the Fox Theater !

FAST routes cover all major destinations of the city: downtown, neighborhoods, shopping areas, and shopping malls.

sections.body:

 A network of local buses connects the uphill and downhill areas with suburban neighbourhoods and green spaces such as Hartsholme Country Park. Taxis and app-based private hire services are easy to find near the bus station, rail station, and Brayford Waterfront, and are particularly useful at night or for avoiding the hill. Cycling is also possible, especially along routes near Brayford Pool and out towards the surrounding countryside.

sections.heading: Megabus recommendation: What to do in Lincoln?
sections.body:

- Walk around Lincoln Castle to experience its medieval walls, Victorian prison, and see an original copy of the Magna Carta. 

- Visit the International Bomber Command Centre to learn about Second World War history through powerful exhibitions and memorial displays. 

- Discover the Museum of Lincolnshire Life to explore local heritage and everyday history, with free entry.

 Other popular attractions include the International Bomber Command Centre, which combines a striking memorial with exhibitions on Second World War history, and the Museum of Lincolnshire Life, which offers insight into local culture and history and is known for free entry.

sections.heading: When to visit Lincoln?
sections.body:
Lincoln can be visited year-round, but late spring through early autumn, roughly April to September, is often the most comfortable time. During these months, the weather is milder, parks and outdoor areas are at their best, and attractions tend to have longer opening hours. 

 Summer brings more visitors and outdoor events, while winter is generally quieter apart from the festive period and the well-known Christmas market season. The weather in this part of England can be changeable at any time of year, so carrying a light waterproof jacket is usually a sensible choice.

Travelers can choose from hotels near the historic Cathedral and Castle quarter, modern stays around the city centre and Brayford Waterfront, as well as budget-friendly hotels slightly outside the core areas. Staying close to the city centre or the waterfront makes it easier to explore major attractions, enjoy local dining spots, and get around comfortably on foot.

sections.body:
Lincoln’s nightlife is lively but contained, with most bars and venues clustered around Brayford Waterfront and the city centre. The presence of the university adds energy, with live music, craft beer, and student nights common. 

 Traditional pubs such as The Cardinal’s Hat offer a more classic atmosphere, particularly in the historic centre. The uphill Cathedral quarter is generally quieter at night, with fewer late-night venues and a calmer feel.

sections.heading: Food and drinks location in Omaha
sections.body:

sections.body:

 Hotels such as Magnolia Hotel Omaha, Hyatt Place Omaha Downtown Old Market, and Moxy Omaha Downtown are popular choices for travelers who want to stay close to the Old Market district and central attractions.

sections.heading: Which Is The Best Time To Visit Omaha?
sections.body:
Omaha experiences four distinct seasons, and the best time to visit often depends on what kind of travel experience you prefer. 

 Most people choose to explore during Spring and fall because these seasons provide ideal weather conditions with mild temperatures and a pleasant climate. The city receives its largest number of visitors during the summer because the College World Series event transforms it into a must-see destination for baseball enthusiasts. 

 The winter season creates a tranquil setting, which brings cold temperatures. Yet this period serves as the best time for travelers who want to avoid crowded areas and find budget-friendly lodging options.

sections.heading: Top Ten Travel Destinations to Visit
sections.body:
###   

### New York City, USA 
 New York is a destination on every person’s bucket list. If you’ve never been to NYC, you should definitely consider visiting the most iconic city in the world. The energy, the culture, and its iconic skyline make New York City an unforgettable place to explore. You’ll get world-famous landmarks like the Statue of Liberty, vibrant neighborhoods like Manhattan, and endless entertainment, especially if you are into Broadway and musicals. The city truly has something to offer, whatever you wish to do on your vacation. Check out our travel guide to New York City for more inspiration, how to get there, and all the right travel tips. 

 Don’t miss: 

- Times Square 

- Central Park 

- The stature of Liberty 

- Brooklyn Bridge 

 Best time to visit: 

 Spring (April to June) and fall (September to November) offer the best weather and are ideal times for sightseeing. If you are planning a Christmas trip, NYC is magical during winter. 

###   

### Paris, France 
 Paris is a dream destination, especially if you love history, art, architecture, and restaurants! It might sound a bit cliché, but Paris is one of those cities you have to visit at least once in your life. You can stroll along the Seine River, explore the charming neighborhoods, visit the iconic landmarks, especially the Eiffel Tower, and shop at Avenue des Champs-Élysées. Paris is the most romantic city in the world, but don’t forget that it also has a lively nightlife. 

 Don’t miss: 

- The Eiffel Tower 

- The Louvre Museum 

- Notre-Dame Cathedral 

- Mountmatre 

 Best time to visit: 

 Spring (April to June) and early fall (September to October) are the best times to visit outside the peak summer months for fewer crowds, blooming gardens, and comfortable weather. 

###   

### Tokyo, Japan 
 Tokyo is the perfect blend of ancient traditions and modern innovation. You can see this in the harmony between peaceful temples and historic neighborhoods, and the neon-lit streets. Japan’s capital offers endless experiences if you wish to discover Japanese culture, visit vibrant places, and eat sushi. Tokyo is one of the top ten travel destinations if you want excitement at every turn. 

 Don’t miss: 

- Shibuya Crossing 

- Senso-ji Temple 

- Tokyo Skytree 

- Tsukiji Outer Market 

 Best time to visit: 

 Spring (March to May) is the cherry blossom season and a popular time to visit because of the mild weather. 

###   

### Bodrum, Turkey 
 If you’re planning a Mediterranean getaway, Turkey’s coastal cities like Antalya and Fethiye are great choices, but Bodrum offers a completely exceptional experience. Located on the Aegean coast, Bodrum offers beautiful beaches, crystal-clear waters, and a relaxed seaside atmosphere. But when you go beyond the coastline and into the city, you’re met with historic landmarks, charming streets, lively marina, and delicious local cuisine. 

 Don’t miss: 

- Bodrum Castle 

- The marina and waterfront restaurants 

- The ancient ruins of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus 

- The beaches of Bitez and Yalıkavak  

 Best time to visit: 

 May to October is the best period to visit Bodrum’s beaches due to the warm weather. Late spring and early fall are also good times to visit to get fewer crowds and more comfortable weather. 

###   

### Rome, Italy 
 No city can match Rome’s combination of history, culture, and cuisine. Known as the Eternal City, Rome gives you the chance to explore ancient ruins, famous landmarks, and beautiful neighborhoods in one unforgettable trip. There’s truly nothing like walking on centuries-old streets and enjoying authentic Italian food in local cafes.

- The Colosseum 

- The Vatican Museums and St. Peter’s Basilica 

- The Trevi Fountain 

- The Pantheon

sections.heading: Top Ten US Ski Vacation Destinations
sections.body:
### Aspen, Colorado 
 Aspen is one of the most famous ski destinations in the US. Its high-level slopes, Rocky Mountain scenery, and vibrant downtown are what attract visitors and have them coming back. Aspen is known for its upscale reputation, but it offers much more than skiing. If you plan a trip to Aspen, you can also take advantage of its art galleries, boutique shops, cozy cafés, and winter events. 

 Best for 

- Intermediate and advanced skiers looking for varied terrain 

- Couples planning a romantic winter getaway 

- Travelers who enjoy lively mountain towns and après-ski activities 

- Visitors looking to combine outdoor adventure with dining, shopping, and culture 

 Know before you go 

- Ski season runs from late November until mid-April. The most reliable snow conditions happen between January and early March. 

- Aspen offers four ski mountains, each with a different skiing experience: Aspen Mountains, Aspen Highlands, Buttermilk, and Snowmass. 

- Downtown Aspen is compact and walkable for exploring restaurants, shops, and galleries. 

### Park City, Utah 
 We can’t have a top ten US ski vacation destinations list and not mention Park City! Simply because the largest ski resort in the US is in Park City, Utah. Although that’s not all: Park City is a favorite among skiers and snowboarders because, with over 7,300 acres of skiable terrain, it offers gentle beginner runs and more challenging slopes for skiers with all experience levels. Apart from skiing, Park City also offers a welcoming atmosphere for all travelers. Its historic Main Street is lined with local boutiques, restaurants, galleries, and year-round events. 

 Best for 

- Families and groups with mixed skiing skills 

- First-time skiers looking for beginner-friendly trails 

- Travelers who want a mix of outdoor adventure and small-town charm 

- Visitors interested in dining, shopping, and local events after a day on the slopes 

 Know before you go 

- Similar to Aspen, ski season runs from late November until mid-April, with peak season around January to March. 

- Park City Mountain offers a variety of runs, terrain parks, and ski schools. 

- Historic Main Street is walkable and perfect for relaxing and shopping between ski sessions. 

- If you’re planning to travel in January, be mindful of the Sundance Film Festival dates. Accommodation and attractions might be busier than usual. 

### Lake Tahoe, California & Nevada 
 Sitting right on the California-Nevada border, Lake Tahoe is one of the most iconic US ski vacation destinations. You’ll get snow-capped mountains and crystal clear water; a unique ski vacation with breathtaking views. You’ll get a variety of terrain, several ski resorts, lakeside towns, cozy restaurants, and outdoor winter activities. 

 Best for 

- Visitors seeking stunning mountain and lake views 

- Travelers looking for a mix of skiing and sightseeing 

- Families, couples, and groups with varied interests 

 Know before you go 

- Ski season runs from late November through April, but check availability. Snowfall varies from year to year. 

- Ski resorts in Lake Tahoe include Palisades Tahoe, Heavenly, Northstar California, and Sierra-at-Tahoe. 

- Check weather forecasts and road updates before traveling because winter road conditions can change quickly. 

### Vail, Colorado 
 Next on our top ten US ski vacation destinations list is Vail, one of the most famous ski destinations in Colorado. Vail is known for its expansive slopes, beautiful mountain scenery, and charming alpine village. Fun fact: Vail is inspired by traditional European ski towns, offering a unique experience without leaving the US. In Vail, you’ll get trails for different ski levels, scenic gondola rides, and plenty of dining and entertainment options. It truly is an ideal destination for every type of winter traveler. 

 Best for 

- Skiers and snowboarders of all experience levels 

- Travelers looking for a more classic European experience 

- Coup

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
What is the best US ski vacation destination? 

 Choosing the best US destination for your ski trip depends on your travel style and ski experience level. In our list, we mentioned the best destinations for different skill levels, resort styles, town vibes, activities, and popularity. 

 When is the best time to plan a ski trip in the US? 

 Generally, ski season is between November and April in the US. Most of the ski destinations are in peak season from January to March due to snowfall levels being the highest. 

 Which US ski destinations are best for beginners? 

 While most ski resorts in the US offer different ski runs for different experience levels, Park City and Breckenridge are popular choices for first-time skiers. They offer beginner-friendly terrain, ski schools, and a welcoming atmosphere. 

 What should I pack for my ski trip? 

 Warm and waterproof clothes are the most important items you should pack. Make sure you have enough layers to stay comfortable and warm. Insulated gloves, ski goggles, sturdy winter boots, and a helmet are also essential items for a ski trip.

sections.heading: Top 5 Things to do on a trip to Toronto
sections.body:
- Explore the Distillery District 

- Ride to the top of CN Tower 

- Bask in the glory of the Hockey Hall of Fame 

- See the animals at the Toronto Zoo 

- Ferry ride to Toronto Islands 

 When on your trip to Toronto, you may realize that the locals are overly friendly, polite, and fashionable – so bring your best clothing and dress to impress.

 Toronto provides an eclectic downtown area with plenty to see and do within walking distance.

 The capital of Ontario and Canada’s largest city, Toronto is littered with historical sights and tours.

 If you’ve never been to Toronto, you owe yourself a proper adventure of exploring the history and culture it provides.

 Numerous tours can help you navigate downtown and there are plenty of parks to explore.

 Throughout Toronto you’ll be able to marvel at historic architecture, have the tough decision of choosing where to eat, visit museums, and much more.

 We’ll try to help simplify your trip to Toronto by providing some our favorite hotels, shops, and restaurants listed below!

sections.heading: Transportation options in Toronto
sections.body:
When you book a bus trip to Toronto with Megabus, you can rest assured knowing you'll be dropped off in the heart of the city. Visit our bus stop page and see our schedules for specific details on where to go to catch your bus.

 A few of our most popular routes in Toronto include:

- Buffalo to Toronto Bus 

- New York to Toronto Bus 

- Detroit to Toronto Bus 

- Rochester to Toronto Bus 

 Upon your arrival, getting around on your trip to Toronto will be a breeze.

 Toronto is one of the most accessible cities in Canada and is set up on a grid street layout , making it easy to navigate by foot.

 There are plenty of transit options via bus and rail such as GO Transit and the Toronto Transit Commission.

 Bicycles are also readily available to rent if you want some exercise. In addition, taxis and ride shares make up a major presence in Toronto.

 Learn more about Megabus' top routes .

sections.heading: Best places to stay in Toronto
sections.body:
After your long exhaustive day of sight-seeing, you’re going to need a place to crash. Toronto is widely known for its amenities and extensive hotel accommodations.

 There are plenty of hotels to choose from, making a trip to Toronto accessible for any traveler.

 The most lavish hotels in Toronto would be the Ritz-Carlton or the Four Seasons Toronto, putting you in a central location to many of the city’s sights.

 Alternatively, many hotels such as the Bond Place Hotel, Super 8 Downtown Toronto, or other rentals are available at a lower cost and offer plenty of travel options for your trip to Toronto.

sections.heading: Nightlife in Toronto
sections.body:
Nightlife in Toronto isn’t exclusive to hipsters. There’s such an explosive scene of live music, bars, and clubs in Toronto that it will be hard to stay in one place.

 If you’re looking for cocktails while on your trip to Toronto, look no further than The Cloak Bar. Boasting an old-school interior and an extensive cocktail menu, The Cloak Bar is a hidden gem tucked away in the Fashion district of downtown Toronto.

 Another great spot for drinks on your trip to Toronto is The Loose Moose Tap and Grill. Many locals flock here for an amazing selection of beers or to catch a game.

 For live music fans, Lee’s Palace is an outstanding venue to round out your Toronto trip.

sections.heading: Where to shop on your trip to Toronto
sections.body:
There will be no shortage of shopping options while you’re in the limits of the city, whether you’re seeking retail therapy or looking to stock up on maple syrup as souvenirs.

 No shopping trip in Toronto would be complete without visiting the historic Distillery District. It serves as a local and tourist favorite spot for urban flair and over 80 shops, boutiques, and restaurants.

 However, you can’t bring up shopping and dining in Toronto without mentioning Kensington Market.

 One of the most vibrant and diverse parts of Toronto, Kensington Market offers a mix of vintage clothing stores, gourmet food stores, cafes, and more.

sections.heading: Best free things to do in Toronto
sections.body:
- High Park 

- Bata Shoe Museum 

- Museum of Contemporary Canadian Art 

- Tour Guys Company Free Walking Tour 

- Graffiti Alley in Toronto 

 Even the most frugal of travelers will find something to love on their trip to Toronto.

 One of the greatest reasons to take a trip to Toronto is that many of the attractions are of no cost to you. 

 Totally free, you owe yourself a trip to High Park, offering near 400 acres of beautiful landscape.

 Consider taking a free walking tour through downtown offered by the Tour Guys Company to learn of Toronto’s history.

 You can even soak in the culture on your trip to Toronto by walking through Graffiti Alley in the Fashion District for some masterfully crafted street art.

 Regular (all-year) bus stop at Canal St: The regular Providence bus stop is on Canal St, between Smith St. and Park Row, across from the Roger William National Park. Seasonal service to/from Seastreak Terminal, Providence Summer weekend service to/from the Providence Seastreak Ferry Terminal operates from the Seastreak Ferry Terminal at 25 India Street. Service to/from this stop is limited. Please check your reservation carefully. Plan your bus trip to Providence

### Boston
 Peter Pan/Megabus Services to All Destinations: All Peter Pan/Megabus sold services to CT, DC, MA, MD, NJ, NY, PA and RI depart from the Peter Pan Bus Gates at the South Station Bus Terminal. Please check the screens at the station for the correct departure gate on arrival at the station. Dattco/Megabus Services to Vermont All megabus sold services to Vermont depart from the Gate 13 (Dattco) at the South Station Bus Terminal. ## ##

## # About Megabus
Megabus offers city-to-city bus tickets for your travel throughout North America, all bookable from your computer or smartphone! Customers keep coming back for our well connected North American transportation network and great bus service from the moment you book to when you arrive safely and quickly at your destination. The Megabus model was designed with the customer in mind, and we can’t wait to hit the road with you!


## ## Where is Megabus?
Almost anywhere you need us to be!

 Explore our most popular routes  and information about  our night buses .

 Megabus has major North American transportation hubs around the US and Canada, serving over 500 different cities and university campuses .

 Megabus helps you stay connected at a great low price for your convenience .


## ## What can you expect with Megabus?
With an expansive network of routes across North America, when you purchase tickets with Megabus, you will be riding in comfort and confidence. 

 We provide options for affordable and reliable bus services, offering the highest level of comfort and safety.

 You can be assured of a great experience and overall satisfaction when you choose Megabus.

 Whether your journey is cross-country or just a mere few cities away, you can rest assured that you are receiving the dependable, quality service you deserve. Our professional customer support staff is here to help you every step of the way to ensure your trip is seamless and stress-free!

 Still not convinced you should book with us? We have so much to offer our customers – here are just a few reasons why you should choose Megabus! 

 Are you looking to partner with Megabus? Learn more about what we have to offer!
